title: Regional fallback operator for stateful downstreams (Redis / Kafka / Postgres)
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Implement a region-aware fallback operator that orchestrates graceful degradation and fast failover for stateful downstreams (Redis, Kafka, Postgres) while preserving SLOs. This ticket covers design, prototype operator, automated tests, and an incremental rollout plan with observability and runbook updates.
background: Recent incidents demonstrated that cross-region topology changes and transient downstream saturation cause cascading tail latency and refresh storms. Existing client-side retries and naive failover cause cache stampedes and split-brain writes for stateful stores. We need a single operator to manage per-region posture: admission control, connection steering, sticky session draining, read-only degrade modes, and circuit-breaker orchestration tailored for Redis, Kafka, and Postgres.
proposed_solution: Create a Kubernetes operator (redwood-fallback-operator) plus a light client library extension. Operator responsibilities:
proposed_solution_list: Maintain a region posture map and health signals from store-side probes and tenant-level SLO telemetry
Drive connection steering rules to a local read replica or cheaper variant when a primary region is degraded
Coordinate per-pool circuit-breaker state (open / closed / half-open) and surface consistent API for clients
Expose per-tenant priority lanes and token-bucket admission to ensure high-priority requests preserve tail SLOs
Trigger automatic read-only mode for Postgres when write-path is at risk, with write-buffering to durable queue (Kafka) as fallback
For Redis, switch to degraded-mode served by a read-through local LRU cache for non-critical keys and prioritized key eviction for ephemeral caches
For Kafka, throttle non-essential consumers and enable fast consumer group rebalance hints to avoid rebalance storms
Provide graceful drain hooks to preserve KV cache snapshots and in-flight message acknowledgements during failover
tradeoffs_and_risks: Operator centralizes control which reduces ad-hoc scripts but increases blast radius. Risk: operator misconfiguration could amplify cross-region failovers. Mitigations include canarying, strict RBAC, conservative defaults, and kill-switch linting in CI.
slo_targets: Platform tail P95 latency <= 200ms for cached reads; P99 <= 800ms for critical routes; system-level availability >= 99.95%. During controlled degrade windows, availability floor is 99.0% with explicit customer notifications.
acceptance_criteria: Canary deploy in staging and trigger simulated region loss without violating critical-route SLOs more than allowed burn rate
Operator exposes /metrics and structured traces for each failover action
Automated chaos tests demonstrate no more than 30% increase in P99 latency for best-effort routes and <5% error rate increase for priority lanes
Runbook updated and on-call run-through performed with SREs
Client library backpressure signals accepted by at least 3 downstream services in staging
rollout_plan: 1) Merge operator core and client patches behind feature flag. 2) Small canary in a dev region (1 tenant). 3) Expand to non-critical tenant cohort and run chaos scenarios (region outage, storage cold restart). 4) Enable for 5% traffic on one critical route with monitoring. 5) Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable metrics.
monitoring_and_alerting: New Grafana dashboard: fallback-operator-overview (per-region health, circuit states, admission rates)
Prometheus alerts: FallbackOperator_OpenCircuitHigh (>5% pools open for 5m), RegionFailoverRate (>1 event / 10m), AdmissionRejectionHigh (>2% of priority lanes)
SLO burn rate alert integration with PagerDuty for >2x burn over 30m
implementation_notes: Prototype operator built in Go using controller-runtime. Client extension provides small API: FallbackPolicy.evaluate(ctx, requestMeta) and BackpressureToken.acquire(ctx, weight). Avoid adding heavy logic to hot path; majority of decisions are cached in operator CRD and served over in-cluster control plane with TTL.
comments: 2025-10-03 Diego Martinez: Initial write-up and architecture sketch uploaded. Tagged SRE and platform-api for early review.
2025-10-08 Grace Liu (SRE): Suggest adding rate-limited write-buffering to Kafka only for customers opting into eventual-write guarantees. Concern: load amplification on buffer drains.
2025-10-15 Aisha Patel: Implemented operator health CRD and basic connection-steer prototype. Opening PR for client changes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fallback-operator/pull/94
2025-10-22 Jonah Becker (Platform API): Reviewed client API. Requested clearer semantics for priority lanes and token accounting. Added unit tests requirement for backpressure edge cases.

2025-10-30 Aisha Patel: Ran staging chaos test (simulate region split). Observed increased P99 on best-effort routes — tuned admission bucket weights and reduced aggressive replica switching. Added follow-up ENG-342345 to optimize Redis eviction policy in degraded mode.
2025-11-05 Diego Martinez: Security review scheduled. Need KMS integration for operator state encryption before production rollout. Created ENG-342210 to track KMS work.
notes: Follow conservative defaults: prefer degraded but serving over hard fails. Keep operator decisions idempotent and observable. Plan to present design to Reliability guild on 2025-11-10.
